plan: This is a second-price auction (highest bidder pays second-highest bid). In second-price auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy - it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bids. Bidding higher than value risks paying more than the item's worth to me if others bid between my value and my bid. Bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. With my value at $23, I should bid exactly $23 to ensure optimal outcomes.

This is a second-price auction, where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. Bidding exactly my value ($18) ensures I never pay more than the item is worth to me, and I maximize my expected profit since overbidding risks paying more than my value, while underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. With no other information about opponents' strategies, truthful bidding is optimal.

This is a second-price auction where bidding my true value is the dominant strategy. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so bidding above my value adds risk of overpaying relative to my value if I'm not truly the highest, while bidding below risks losing profitable opportunities. Bidding exactly $39 ensures I win whenever profitable (when others bid less than $39) and never overpay since I only pay the second-highest bid.
